newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen priced at $66-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen priced at $66-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle owners were seen pricing cattle at $66.00 per cwt on Monday amid outlooks for firm prices next week, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were light at $64.00, but passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00 to $66.00. Cattle this week traded at $64.00 in active sales, steady with last week, they said.
Most showlists sold out, which gave optimism to owners as feedlots were able to remain current, the sources said.
Fed cattle prices next week also were seen bolstered by projections for steady to smaller numbers of market-ready cattle on new showlists, they said.
Fed cattle prices also could be underpinned by continued strength in boxed beef, particularly if slaughter is light, the feedlot sources said.

Cattle slaughter this week was pegged at 701,000 head, down 2.4 percent from last week, USDA statisticss showed. Beef production for the week ending Saturday was estimated down 2.0 percent from a week ago, the statistics showed.
Beef prices this week were underpinned by the light slaughter and production and retail "fill-in" buying for features at the end of the month, which is a week from Thursday, market sources said.
Heavyweight choice beef at midday was quoted at $104.15, up $0.88 from Wednesday and up $5.11 since July 11 when prices begain climbing, USDA statistics showed.
